threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still use an umbrella for the drizzle; true locals just accept the wet and sport a raincoat with pride.
Last night on the 333, a guy serenaded the bus with 'Don't Stop Believin''—we all joined in. Only in Brixton, right?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I realized I was home when I saw the elderly couple at the bakery, arguing over who gets the last Stückchen of the best Käsekuchen. Classic Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg do you find spontaneous street parties popping up from nothing, with just a DJ and a few boomboxes. It’s like the city gives permission to celebrate life at any moment.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only a local would know that the burrito’s true test is whether it can survive a BART delay. Out-of-towners just stroll by, blissfully unaware.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy on the 6 Rapid passionately arguing with a pigeon about the best pizza in the city. Never seen that level of commitment before.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think 'patatas bravas' are just fried potatoes; you can tell a local by how they debate the sauce's spice level over a morning café.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They still ask for pa amb tomàquet at cafés instead of just ordering ‘toast with tomato’. It’s the little things that give them away.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still stand waiting for the bus at the stop instead of knowing to just walk down the street to catch it at the next crossing.
Last night on the 77, a guy in a full tuxedo argued with the driver about the route. No idea where he was heading, but the whole bus seemed invested.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I heard a group of kids swapping stories about their grandparents' bakery in Turkish, I realized this place has layers that run deep.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin do you find a café that doubles as a pet adoption center—grab a coffee while cats roam freely, looking for homes!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by their reaction to BART delays—it's just a shrug and a resigned laugh, not panic like the newcomers.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy dressed as a hot dog trying to explain to Muni drivers why the bus couldn't move. Meanwhile, the dog on the tracks was just chilling.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about the parks, but it's really the little bodega conversations over vermut that define our vibe.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their hesitation at the metro ticket machines. They still scan for prices like it’s a luxury item instead of a daily travel necessity.
